parts.note: a household cleaning tool made of plumes, which only flicks lightly over surfaces

explanation.surface: Praise for a gentle housekeeper who barely brushes the furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' suggests a person employed to clean; it is the implement, and the light touch is its feathery tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description of a plume-tipped duster that removes dust with the gentlest contact.

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or laid waste, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Root vegetables left to rot on a mountain slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' shuffles SWEDES and LIE. 'Alpine' is a noun here: a plant of the high mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The white-flowered plant is the best-known example of an alpine, a mountain plant.

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words pretty rolling

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the alpine plant grows here among scenic rolling hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue, so 'here' means the Alpine region where the flower grows.
explanation.definitionFit: An Austrian Alpine province, so it is a place fitting 'here' after the alpine plant clue.

clue.text: Digger up of bodies — once sounded fun

parts.note: once means former, ex-

indicators.note: sounded signals that a word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: fun means humour or comedy

explanation.surface: A gravedigger who used to be a joker.
explanation.walkthrough: HUMER is how HUMOUR sounds in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: One who exhumes digs corpses back out of the grave, a literal description.

clue.text: Nymphs run through the backs of sundry glades

indicators.note: only the rear portions of the two words are kept, their fronts discarded

explanation.surface: Woodland spirits dashing through various forest clearings.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the back parts DRY (of sundry) and ADES (of glades); the nymphs 'run through' them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree nymphs of Greek myth, plural, matching the plural nymphs.

clue.text: They fix TVs and production units

parts.note: television receivers are TV sets
film or stage production teams are crews

explanation.surface: Engineers who repair televisions and factory equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Small screws used to hold parts firmly in place, so things that fasten.

clue.text: A bird nesting finally in fallen tree

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
a fallen tree lies wrecked, so its letters are rearranged
finally picks the closing letter of nesting

explanation.surface: A bird building its nest in a toppled tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fallen' turns TREE into ERET, and 'finally' takes G from nesting, which 'in' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A white heron, a wading bird species.

parts.note: a cricket fielder in the slips position who keeps dropping catches

explanation.surface: Describing a careless mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' looks like an error but is a cricket fielding position close behind the batter; a clumsy one drops the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial term for someone who fumbles and drops things, such as a fielder spilling catches.

parts.note: a printed table of ready-made calculations, the kind a cash-handling trader would consult

explanation.surface: Asks about the counter money dealers worked at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' suggests furniture, like the moneychangers' tables in the Temple; it is a printed chart of sums. 'Ready' is also slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of precalculated figures for quick arithmetic, used by traders handling money.

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters being played about with, rearranged

explanation.surface: A ghost strumming a harp, as angels are said to.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean otherworldly, not of this earth.

indicators.note: design here means the word great is reshaped into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A shield of impressive craftsmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round shield of the kind carried by Highland soldiers.

clue.text: It's thrown in to beat the bell

definitions.text: It's thrown in to beat the bell

parts.words: It's thrown in to beat the bell
parts.note: in boxing a corner concedes by tossing this cloth into the ring before the round ends

explanation.surface: Something tossed into a contest before the final bell rings.
explanation.walkthrough: In boxing, a second throws a towel into the ring to concede; the bell would end the round.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing in the towel is the boxing gesture of surrender, an idiom for giving up.

clue.text: Drugged caddie met with rough treatment

indicators.note: rough treatment knocks the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A golf caddie is roughed up and sedated.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated with medicine, so given drugs.

clue.text: Bird — robin in UK, roadrunner in US

parts.note: the rail is a family of wading birds
the Reliant Robin was a small three-wheeled British car

explanation.surface: A naturalist comparing birds on either side of the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'robin' and 'roadrunner' look like birds; the Robin is a British car, and Americans call the railway a railroad, so a self-propelled carriage running on it is a 'roadrunner'.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled railway carriage runs on what Americans call the railroad.

clue.text: Clipped two dogs (last two of breed)

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to dog someone is to follow, or tail, them

indicators.note: last two of takes the final pair of letters of breed

explanation.surface: Two dogs had their tails docked, considering their breeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dogs' does double duty in the surface: read once as a noun for the mongrel and once as a verb, since to dog someone is to shadow them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut short, as when something is reduced or trimmed back.

definitions.meaning: the first name of the Hollywood actor Tracy, belonging to him
an old word for a type of wig, also a short jacket

explanation.surface: Asks whether an actor's hair is his own.
explanation.walkthrough: Spencer Tracy was a Hollywood star; the name is also an old word for a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor's first name and an archaic term for a kind of periwig.

clue.text: Like singing sailor in tin hat

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: in places the sailor inside the hat

parts.note: tile is slang for a hat
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor in a tin helmet bursting into song.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE is old slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning in a smooth, singing style.

parts.note: loose leaflets tucked into a newspaper that fall out when it is opened

explanation.surface: Asks about people who quit each day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' is a newspaper, not a frequency; 'drop-outs' are the flyers that slip from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose advertising leaflets placed inside a newspaper, which tend to fall out.

clue.text: Put in post at suite, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints at another possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone stationed at a hotel suite.
explanation.definitionFit: To situate is to place or locate, as in putting someone in a position.

clue.text: Dixon's fellow linesman in charge of the lodge

parts.note: Mason and Dixon surveyed the Mason-Dixon line together

explanation.surface: A surveyor colleague put in charge of a lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon drew the US boundary called the Mason-Dixon line.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Freemasons, whose local branch is called a lodge.

parts.note: the bird's name sounds like the two words Arab who with an extra M at the front, so they rhyme

explanation.surface: An Arab poet rhyming lines about a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, 'Arab who' rhymes with the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A large African stork, whose feathers are also used for trimming.

clue.text: Girl, a brat, chewing up the rock

indicators.note: chewing up mangles the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A spoilt girl gnawing on a stick of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' looks like confectionery; it is the Rock, the British territory at the mouth of the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Popularly called the Rock, after its great limestone promontory.

indicators.note: noisy says the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a byre is a cowshed

explanation.surface: Someone buying a shed full of lowing cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyer is one who purchases.

clue.text: It's played in the Caspian on water

indicators.note: in signals letters lying inside the words Caspian on

explanation.surface: Music performed on a boat on the Caspian Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument, which is played.

indicators.note: following puts the apprentice after the fairy

parts.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian myth
L for learner, as on L-plates, means an apprentice

explanation.surface: A trainee chasing a fairy into a dangerous place.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is serious danger or risk.

parts.note: Roy is a man's name
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: Two men building a sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A light sail set above the topgallant on a square-rigged ship.

indicators.note: in puts the popular word inside the inn

parts.note: an auberge is a French inn
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A fruit that is a hit at a French inn.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the eggplant is a fruit, a berry.

indicators.note: after places Bob behind the game

parts.note: bridge is a card game
Bob the Builder is a children's TV character

explanation.surface: Someone joining Bob after a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob the Builder is a British children's animated TV character.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaphorically one who brings opposing sides together, linking them.
